title: RS_MakeRaster
description: >
  Creates a one-band out-of-database raster that references a band of a raster
  file, from a path, pixel type and grid definition alone. Nothing is read from
  the file: the result is built without any I/O, and the pixels are loaded
  lazily when a function needs them.
kernels:
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - name: path
      type: string
      description: >
        Path or URL of the raster file, in any form RS_FromPath accepts. This is
        the bare file location: select the band with the band argument, not a
        `#band=` fragment (a path containing one is an error).
    - name: band_data_type
      type: string
      description: >
        Pixel type of the band in the file: int8, uint8, int16, uint16, int32,
        uint32, int64, uint64, float32 or float64; Sedona Spark's letter codes
        (D, F, I, UI, S, US, B); or an RS_BandPixelType name such as
        UNSIGNED_8BITS.
    - name: width
      type: integer
      description: Raster width in pixels.
    - name: height
      type: integer
      description: Raster height in pixels.
    - name: extent
      type: geometry
      description: >
        The raster covers this geometry's envelope with north-up pixels, and its
        CRS is the geometry's. Only correct when the file's grid is north-up and
        in the geometry's CRS. A geography is accepted too, in which case the
        envelope follows spherical edges and comes from the session's geography
        bounder, as for RS_MakeEmptyRaster.
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - name: path
      type: string
    - name: band_data_type
      type: string
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
    - name: extent
      type: geometry
    - name: band
      type: integer
      description: >
        1-based index of the band in the file to reference. Defaults to 1.
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - name: path
      type: string
    - name: band_data_type
      type: string
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
    - name: upper_left_x
      type: double
      description: X coordinate of the upper-left corner of the upper-left pixel.
    - name: upper_left_y
      type: double
      description: Y coordinate of the upper-left corner of the upper-left pixel.
    - name: scale_x
      type: double
      description: Pixel width.
    - name: scale_y
      type: double
      description: Pixel height; negative for a north-up raster.
    - name: skew_x
      type: double
      description: Rotation/shear term of the x coordinate.
    - name: skew_y
      type: double
      description: Rotation/shear term of the y coordinate.
    - name: crs
      type: integer
      description: >
        The raster's CRS: an integer EPSG code (0 for no CRS), or a CRS string
        such as 'EPSG:32627', PROJJSON or WKT, as accepted by RS_SetCRS.
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - name: path
      type: string
    - name: band_data_type
      type: string
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
    - name: upper_left_x
      type: double
    - name: upper_left_y
      type: double
    - name: scale_x
      type: double
    - name: scale_y
      type: double
    - name: skew_x
      type: double
    - name: skew_y
      type: double
    - name: crs
      type: string
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - name: path
      type: string
    - name: band_data_type
      type: string
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
    - name: upper_left_x
      type: double
    - name: upper_left_y
      type: double
    - name: scale_x
      type: double
    - name: scale_y
      type: double
    - name: skew_x
      type: double
    - name: skew_y
      type: double
    - name: crs
      type: integer
    - name: band
      type: integer
  - returns: raster
    args:
    - name: path
      type: string
    - name: band_data_type
      type: string
    - name: width
      type: integer
    - name: height
      type: integer
    - name: upper_left_x
      type: double
    - name: upper_left_y
      type: double
    - name: scale_x
      type: double
    - name: scale_y
      type: double
    - name: skew_x
      type: double
    - name: skew_y
      type: double
    - name: crs
      type: string
    - name: band
      type: integer
---

## Description

`RS_MakeRaster` builds an out-of-database raster with the grid, CRS and pixel
type that [`RS_FromPath`](rs_frompath.qmd) would read for one band of a file,
but from its arguments instead of the file's header. The result has a single
band that references band `band` of `path`; its grid is either:

- **the envelope of an extent geometry**, covered by `width` x `height`
  north-up pixels, with the geometry's CRS; or
- **a full affine transform and CRS**, given as the six geotransform
  parameters and an EPSG code or CRS string. The transform must be finite and
  invertible (`scale_x * scale_y - skew_x * skew_y` not zero).

`RS_MakeRaster` records no nodata value, even when the file has one. Until
[`RS_SetBandNoDataValue`](rs_setbandnodatavalue.qmd) sets it, pixel functions
treat nodata differently from a raster from `RS_FromPath`: the file's nodata
pixels count as ordinary values, so statistics such as `RS_SummaryStats`
include them. Set it from the catalog (e.g. STAC's `raster:bands[].nodata`) to
get the same results as `RS_FromPath`; like `RS_MakeRaster` itself,
`RS_SetBandNoDataValue` only changes metadata and does not read the file.

`RS_FromPath` opens every file to read its header, which on object storage
costs at least one request per file. Raster catalogs such as
[stac-geoparquet](https://github.com/stac-utils/stac-geoparquet) already
record each file's grid (the STAC projection extension's `proj:shape`,
`proj:transform` and `proj:code`) and pixel type (`data_type`), so
`RS_MakeRaster` can build the same raster from those columns with no I/O at
all. Functions that only use raster metadata (`RS_Width`, `RS_Envelope`,
`RS_Intersects`, ...) never touch the file; functions that need pixels load
them from `path` when they run, exactly as for a raster from `RS_FromPath`.

::: callout-warning
`RS_MakeRaster` trusts its arguments. Nothing is checked against the file,
not even that it exists, until a function loads its pixels. Wrong metadata is
then caught only in part:

- a wrong `band_data_type` makes the pixel load fail with an error naming the
  file's actual type;
- a `width` or `height` larger than the file's makes the pixel load fail with
  an out-of-bounds read error, while a smaller one silently reads only the
  upper-left `width` x `height` window of the file;
- a wrong grid or CRS is never detected: the pixels are read correctly but
  placed in the wrong location.
:::

The extent form is only correct when the file's grid is north-up and its CRS
is the extent geometry's CRS. A STAC item's `geometry` is always in
longitude/latitude (CRS84), so it describes the grid only for files that are
themselves in longitude/latitude; for anything else, such as an item in a UTM
zone, use the affine form with the item's `proj:transform` and `proj:code`.

Null arguments yield a null raster.

## Examples

Build a raster from stac-geoparquet columns with the affine form. STAC's
`proj:transform` is in affine order `[a, b, c, d, e, f]`, that is
`[scale_x, skew_x, upper_left_x, skew_y, scale_y, upper_left_y]`, and
`proj:shape` is `[height, width]`:

```sql
WITH items AS (
  SELECT
    named_struct(
      'red', named_struct('href', 's3://bucket/scene/B04.tif', 'data_type', 'uint16')
    ) AS assets,
    [10980, 10980] AS "proj:shape",
    [10.0, 0.0, 399960.0, 0.0, -10.0, 4800000.0] AS "proj:transform",
    'EPSG:32627' AS "proj:code"
)
SELECT
  RS_Width(r) AS width, RS_Height(r) AS height,
  RS_UpperLeftX(r) AS ulx, RS_UpperLeftY(r) AS uly, RS_ScaleY(r) AS scale_y,
  RS_CRS(r) AS crs
FROM (
  SELECT RS_MakeRaster(
    assets['red']['href'],
    assets['red']['data_type'],
    "proj:shape"[2], "proj:shape"[1],
    "proj:transform"[3], "proj:transform"[6],
    "proj:transform"[1], "proj:transform"[5],
    "proj:transform"[2], "proj:transform"[4],
    "proj:code"
  ) AS r
  FROM items
);
```

A 400 x 400 grid over a longitude/latitude bounding box, referencing band 2:

```sql
SELECT RS_Envelope(
  RS_MakeRaster(
    's3://bucket/image.tif', 'uint8', 400, 400,
    ST_MakeEnvelope(-120, 30, -110, 40, 4326), 2
  )
);
```

Reading pixels loads them from the file, so for a file whose metadata matches
the arguments (and that has no nodata value, or once `RS_SetBandNoDataValue`
has set it) the result is the same as with `RS_FromPath`:

```sql
SELECT
  RS_Value(
    RS_MakeRaster(
      '../../../submodules/sedona-testing/data/raster/test4.tiff', 'uint8',
      10, 10, ST_MakeEnvelope(0, 0, 10, 10, 4326)
    ),
    ST_Point(5.5, 4.5, 4326)
  ) AS made,
  RS_Value(
    RS_FromPath('../../../submodules/sedona-testing/data/raster/test4.tiff'),
    ST_Point(5.5, 4.5, 4326)
  ) AS read;
```

::: callout-note
Sedona Spark has an `RS_MakeRaster(raster, type, data)` that builds an
in-database raster from a reference raster and an array of pixel values.
SedonaDB's `RS_MakeRaster` shares the name but not the arguments: its forms
start with a path string, so they cannot be confused with that form.
:::
